mechanism_inventory: stale accounting snapshot — balanceBefore computed before weth.approve
missing invariant enforcement — no cap on amount vs actual weth balance held
reward/index update ordering — weth.approve issued before the external call (approval window during call)
hook caller/timing mismatch — _executeEth withdraws ETH then calls target
precision/normalization edge — remainingAfterCall underflow if target drains more than amount
access-control mismatch — execute() is onlyOwner (owner set in constructor)
external-call failure / DoS — weth.withdraw then payable(from).transfer reverts if from rejects ETH

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: In _executeWeth, weth.approve(target, amount) is called before target.call(callPayload). target is arbitrary and user-supplied. After approval, target can call weth.transferFrom(executor, target, amount) inside callPayload OR later (approval persists; never reset). If target consumes 0 during the call, remainingAfterCall = amount and weth.transfer(from, amount) refunds fully while the approval is still live; on a later funded message the lingering approval drains the new WETH — double-spend.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: A malicious target contract. The executor owner (bridge relay) calls execute(from, target=malicious, ...). The malicious contract does not consume the approval during the call; later it drains via the persisted approval.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Attacker controls contract M. 2. owner calls execute(from=A, target=M, deliverEth=false, amount=X, callPayload). 3. _executeWeth: balanceBefore; weth.approve(M,X); M.call returns success consuming 0. remainingAfterCall=X; weth.transfer(A,X). 4. weth.approve(M,X) still active. 5. Next bridge message funds the executor. 6. M calls weth.transferFrom(executor, attacker, X) draining the new deposit. Net: A refunded and attacker drains subsequent deposit.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Bridge users / future depositors whose WETH is drained by the lingering approval.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Persistent weth approval never revoked after _executeWeth — direct source-backed vector (approve with no reset).

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: In _executeEth, weth.withdraw(amount) converts WETH to ETH, then on target failure payable(from).transfer(amount) forwards only 2300 gas. If from is a smart-contract wallet (common cross-chain), transfer reverts, making the bridge message permanently unexecutable (stuck/undeliverable funds).
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: No active attacker needed — a legitimate user whose from is a contract wallet (or a griefer crafting an always-reverting target) triggers permanent undeliverability.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. execute(from=contractWallet, target=T, deliverEth=true, amount=X), gasCurrencyIsEth=true. 2. weth.withdraw(X). 3. T.call{value:X} fails. 4. payable(contractWallet).transfer(X) reverts (>2300 gas needed). 5. Whole execute reverts; message never deliverable for that from.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: User whose funds are bridged but cannot be delivered — bridge message permanently unexecutable for contract from addresses.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Stuck-funds / permanent DoS for a class of users; clears Medium; different actor/state from the approval mechanism.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: remainingAfterCall underflow when target drains more WETH than amount via the approve
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: remainingAfterCall = amount - (balanceBefore - weth.balanceOf(this)); if target pulls > amount (executor holds extra), underflow reverts.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Can executor hold extra WETH beyond amount at call time (dust/failed refunds)? If yes, target can force arithmetic revert, blocking the message.
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Bridge users — undeliverable message, WETH locked.

unresolved_mechanisms.mechanism: Lingering weth approval across multiple execute() calls
unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: weth.approve(target, amount) never reset to 0 after _executeWeth.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Does WETH use standard ERC20 approve (overwrite) so accumulation doesn't apply, or can residuals after partial consumption be drained?
unresolved_mechanisms.who_loses: Future depositors whose WETH flows through the executor.

rejected_mechanisms.mechanism: access-control mismatch on execute() — permissionless entry
rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: execute() has onlyOwner (Owned(msg.sender)); only the owner (bridge relay) can call it.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: No unprivileged caller can invoke execute() directly.

rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: No state deletion or self-destruct present; writes bounded to weth transfers/approvals within execute paths.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: No code path permits unauthorized deletion.

impact_direction.attacker_receives: WETH drained from executor via lingering approval — attacker controlling target extracts WETH from subsequent bridge deposits.
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Attacker's own position unaffected; attack is on other users' bridged funds.
impact_direction.victim_loses: Bridge users lose WETH — drained by approval exploit or permanently stuck (undeliverable message for contract from).
impact_direction.invariant_violated: Cross-chain value conservation: WETH into executor must be delivered to the recipient or returned to sender — approval vector lets a third party drain subsequent deposits; ETH-stuck vector makes delivery impossible for contract from.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: Approval exploit targets other users' funds; stuck-funds affects any cross-chain transfer where from is a contract; neither dust nor admin-only.

stop_condition: more_mechanisms_pending: persistent approval + stuck-funds/DoS carried; underflow + approval accumulation unresolved
